title: AWS Containers Handbook: ECR, ECS, Fargate and EKS
summary: Quick revision notes on running containers on AWS: pushing images to ECR, defining and running ECS tasks and services, choosing Fargate or EC2, IAM roles, EKS, service discovery, load balancers and CloudWatch logs.

chapters.title: ECR and ECS Mental Model
points: ECR is a private per-region registry; an image URI is <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/<repo>:<tag>
ECS hierarchy: cluster holds services; a service keeps N copies of a task; a task is the running instance of a task definition
Task definition is a versioned, immutable JSON blueprint (family:revision); any change creates a new revision
Container definitions inside a task share one network namespace and lifecycle: put tightly coupled containers in one task, everything else in separate tasks
Mistake: using the :latest tag; mutable tags make rollbacks impossible, so tag by git SHA and enable tag immutability

chapters.title: Task Definitions and Services
points: Key task definition fields: family, cpu and memory (task level), networkMode (awsvpc for Fargate), containerDefinitions, taskRoleArn, executionRoleArn
Container essentials: image, portMappings, essential flag (an essential container exiting stops the whole task), environment, secrets (from SSM or Secrets Manager), logConfiguration
Service scheduler: desiredCount, rolling update with minimumHealthyPercent and maxPercent, deployment circuit breaker with rollback
Service auto scaling: target tracking on CPU, memory or ALB RequestCountPerTarget via Application Auto Scaling
Mistake: a task stuck in PROVISIONING or STOPPED with CannotPullContainerError, usually no route to ECR (private subnet without NAT or VPC endpoints) or a missing execution role permission

chapters.title: Fargate vs EC2 and IAM Roles
points: Fargate is serverless: you pay per vCPU and GB per second, with no instances to patch; EC2 launch type means you manage the container instance fleet and its ASG capacity provider
Comparison: Fargate suits most web services and batch work; EC2 suits GPUs, daemon tasks, very large steady workloads and cheaper Spot or Reserved capacity
Execution role is used by ECS itself to pull the ECR image, fetch secrets and write logs to CloudWatch; trust principal ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
Task role is what your application code assumes through the credentials endpoint to call S3, DynamoDB and other AWS APIs, so grant least privilege here
Mistake: putting S3 permissions on the execution role (app gets AccessDenied) or putting ECR pull permission on the task role (task fails to start)

chapters.title: EKS Basics and When to Choose It
points: EKS is managed Kubernetes: AWS runs the control plane (API server, etcd) and you run worker capacity as managed node groups, self-managed nodes or Fargate profiles
Core objects: Pod (smallest unit), Deployment (replicas and rollouts), Service (stable virtual IP), Ingress (HTTP routing, backed by the AWS Load Balancer Controller)
Pod access to AWS uses IRSA or EKS Pod Identity, the EKS equivalent of an ECS task role

Choose ECS when you are AWS-only and want the least operational overhead; choose EKS for Kubernetes portability, the Helm and operator ecosystem, or an existing team skill set; EKS adds a control plane fee per cluster per hour
Mistake: picking EKS for a simple app, then paying in upgrade work (Kubernetes version every ~14 months of support), add-ons and networking complexity

chapters.title: Discovery, Load Balancers, Logs and Commands
points: Service discovery: ECS Service Connect or Cloud Map gives tasks a private DNS name (svc.namespace) so services call each other without a load balancer
ALB integration: the service registers task IPs in a target group (target type ip for awsvpc); health check path and grace period (healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds) decide when tasks are killed
Security groups: ALB group allows 80/443 from the internet; the task group allows the container port only from the ALB group

Logs: awslogs driver in logConfiguration sends stdout and stderr to a CloudWatch log group (options awslogs-group, awslogs-region, awslogs-stream-prefix); the log group must exist and the execution role needs logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents

Everyday commands: aws ecr get-login-password | docker login, docker push, aws ecs register-task-definition, aws ecs update-service --force-new-deployment, aws ecs execute-command for a shell, aws logs tail --follow

chapters.title: AWS Containers Cheat Sheet
points: Flow: build image, push to ECR, register task definition revision, update service, ALB health check passes, traffic shifts
Execution role = pull image, secrets, logs; task role = app AWS API calls
Fargate = no servers, awsvpc networking, per-second billing; EC2 = GPUs, Spot, full host control
Task will not start: check CannotPullContainerError (NAT or endpoints), execution role, and missing log group
Targets unhealthy or tasks cycling: check health check path, grace period, container port, and task security group source
